newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Catholic bishop of Sulu was gunned down by unidentified gunmen in front of the Jolo Cathedral. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Fidel Ramos approved the extension of the suspension of military operations against left-wing rebels for another 30 days to facilitate the completion of the peace process between the government and the communist groups. (BULLETIN/INQUIRER/STAR)

- President Ramos said he was disappointed by the Supreme Court's decision voiding the sale of the Manila Hotel to a Malaysian firm, since it would set back the government's privatisation programme. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Exports grew 17.7 percent to the equivalent of $20.53 billion last year from $17.45 billion in 1995, the National Statistics Office reported. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co said it has filed a petition with the National Telecommunications Commission for a 20 percent reduction in international calls and a 45 percent increase in domestic phone charges. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said the depreciation of the yen from 114.9 to 121.4 against the U.S. dollar from year-end 1996 to February has reduced Philippine foreign debt by $570 million. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
